page.text:
Induction and recursion are dual aspects of the successor structure.
Induction proves that a property holds at every stage; recursion defines
an object at a stage from the objects already defined at earlier stages.
Both principles depend on the absence of hidden natural numbers beyond
those generated from zero by repeated succession.
